findings.description: The start-up sequence says it transmits the code 8 report after any reset. SYS-SUP-034 requires that report when the reset cause is classified as IWDG or WWDG; a power-on, software or other reset does not meet that condition.
findings.requested_change: Make transmission of the code 8 report conditional on classification of a watchdog reset.

findings.description: The element says it answers requests within 50 ms and sends fault reports within 10 ms without the exceptions in its sources. SYS-SUP-063 extends the answer deadline by intervening fault-report transmission time, and SYS-SUP-039 waives the original fault report when a watchdog reset interrupts handling before both report and safe-state entry complete.
findings.requested_change: State the answer-deadline extension and the watchdog-interruption exception for fault reports.

findings.description: The interface states an unconditional 50 ms answer deadline and 10 ms fault-report deadline. SYS-SUP-063 extends the answer deadline by intervening fault-report transmission time; SYS-SUP-039 permits the original report to be omitted when watchdog reset interrupts handling before both reporting and safe-state entry complete.
findings.requested_change: Specify the deadline extension and watchdog-interruption exception in the interface timing and error behavior.

findings.description: The reset path limits the watchdog-interruption case to a reset before the report completes. SYS-SUP-029 and SYS-SUP-039 also cover a watchdog reset after report completion but before safe-state entry completes.
findings.requested_change: Describe the exception for a watchdog reset before both the report and safe-state entry have completed.

findings.description: The CRC peripheral is allocated CRC-32/MPEG-2 computation, but OP-SYE-002 acknowledges that its ability to implement the required algorithm is not established. CON-SUP-003 establishes peripheral availability, not its algorithm support; the hardware allocation and HSI therefore lack an established basis.
findings.requested_change: Establish the peripheral capability from an identified source or provide a supported alternative allocation, and align the open point and CRC interface with that decision.

findings.description: The verification environment is said to provide observation of pins, serial line and reset flags, but CON-SUP-005 establishes the Renode platform and host tooling without establishing those individual capabilities. Reset-flag and output observations are needed to exercise the watchdog and safe-state elements.
findings.requested_change: Identify evidence or a concrete test-environment mechanism for each claimed observation point; record any unresolved capability as an open point.

findings.description: The element says CRC-32/MPEG-2 is computed in software and the peripheral is not relied upon, but interface SYE-SUP-052 describes the CRC peripheral as producing that value for the checks. CON-SUP-003 establishes the peripheral's availability, not that capability.
findings.requested_change: Make the CRC allocation and interface consistent with the supported software computation, and make any peripheral acceleration conditional on evidence of its capability.

findings.description: The start-up sequence drives the status signal high after the checks pass and the latch is clear, without requiring that no fault has been detected since reset. SYS-SUP-028 includes that condition.
findings.requested_change: Include the no-fault-since-reset condition in the start-up transition to operational status.

findings.description: The diagnostic element says a fault report never interrupts an answer line, but does not require it to be sent before subsequent answer lines. SYS-SUP-074 requires that ordering.
findings.requested_change: Specify that a fault report due during an answer line follows that line's line feed and precedes any further line of the answer.

findings.description: The reset interface covers watchdog timeouts but gives only the software-reset request timing. SYS-SUP-011 and SYS-SUP-012 define the independent watchdog timeout and window watchdog timing needed to characterize the watchdog reset paths.
findings.requested_change: State the applicable watchdog timeout and refresh-window timing for the reset paths, with their conditions.

findings.description: The diagnostic interface names RST and FLT fields but does not specify their value ranges or the start-up RST deadline. SYS-SUP-037 defines the reset-cause values and 10 ms deadline; SYS-SUP-040 and SYS-SUP-042 define fault-code and timestamp values.
findings.requested_change: Specify the message field values and timestamp range, and the start-up RST transmission deadline relative to reset-cause classification.

findings.description: SYE-SUP-004 states that software produces the CRC value and the peripheral is unused until capability is established, but its listed interface SYE-SUP-052 unconditionally identifies the CRC peripheral as the hardware endpoint producing that value. CON-SUP-003 establishes peripheral availability, not CRC-32/MPEG-2 capability.
findings.requested_change: Make the element and interface consistently represent the supported software computation and any conditional peripheral use, with hardware capability supported by evidence.

findings.description: SYE-SUP-020 starts alive supervision only after both integrity checks pass and the safe-state latch is clear. SYS-SUP-009 requires alive supervision to start when the checks pass and does not make that action conditional on the latch.
findings.requested_change: Align the start of alive supervision with SYS-SUP-009, or resolve the conflicting conditions in the upstream requirements.

findings.description: SYE-SUP-028 describes GET FAULTS as returning the last eight reports but omits SYS-SUP-081's requirement to fix the answer to reports made before request reception. A report arriving during transmission could otherwise change the answer contents.
findings.requested_change: Specify that the answer contains the qualifying history as of request reception and excludes reports made afterward.

findings.description: SYE-SUP-057 asserts that withholding refresh causes a window watchdog reset by the 12 ms limit. SYS-SUP-012 specifies reset when a refresh arrives too early or too late; it does not establish a reset on absence of a refresh or its deadline.
findings.requested_change: Support the no-refresh reset behavior and deadline with an applicable source, or record the unresolved hardware behavior as an open point and remove the unsupported assertion.

findings.description: The STS field range refers to SYS-SUP-045 and SYS-SUP-049, which specify the GET STATUS answer and ERR behavior, respectively, rather than the state values and fault-count meaning. The interface therefore does not identify those fields' ranges or valid definitions.
findings.requested_change: Specify the STS state values and fault-count meaning using the applicable requirements, including SYS-SUP-046 through SYS-SUP-047 and SYS-SUP-067 through SYS-SUP-069.

findings.description: SYE-SUP-020 lists SYE-SUP-052, the hardware CRC interface, for its start-up checks. SYE-SUP-004 says that interface is conditional and SYE-SUP-065 supplies the software CRC computation, but SYE-SUP-020 does not list SYE-SUP-065. The stated connection therefore conflicts with the chosen computation for SYS-SUP-016 and SYS-SUP-018.
findings.requested_change: Align the start-up manager's interface references with the software CRC path and make any conditional hardware path consistent with the peripheral's stated use.

findings.description: SYE-SUP-064 says it computes the CRC for run-time integrity checks but cites only the start-up requirements SYS-SUP-016 and SYS-SUP-018 and CON-SUP-129. SYS-SUP-066 specifies the whole-image run-time CRC across segments and is not traced to this computation.
findings.requested_change: Trace the run-time computation to its applicable run-time requirements and identify its responsibility for the whole-image CRC across segments.

findings.description: SYE-SUP-065 specifies bytes in and a CRC value out but gives no timing or interaction for the run-time check. SYS-SUP-021 requires one segment per control cycle, SYS-SUP-066 requires one CRC over the whole image, and SYS-SUP-022 limits the check to 0.5 ms per cycle. The interface does not describe how computation continues across segments or fits that timing.
findings.requested_change: Specify the run-time interaction and preservation of CRC state across segments, together with the applicable timing constraints; trace the interface to the relevant run-time requirements.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-033 requires the latch, per-code detection counts and fault history to survive software and watchdog resets. SYE-SUP-025 assigns retention to software, but the architecture identifies no reset-retentive storage element or interface. OP-SYE-001 defers that hardware allocation to software architecture.
findings.requested_change: Identify and allocate a suitable retained-storage element and its access interface, with the reset and power-loss behavior required by the sources. If the necessary hardware choice requires a human decision, make the open point blocking.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-015 requires fault-free start-up without either watchdog resetting. SYE-SUP-020 and SYE-SUP-027 state the outcome, but OP-SYS-002 leaves window-watchdog handling before the first control cycle unresolved. The architecture does not establish a start-up sequence that meets the watchdog window while integrity checks run.
findings.requested_change: Specify a feasible start-up sequence and watchdog servicing or activation strategy, supported by the platform evidence; make the unresolved decision blocking if it cannot be established at this stage.

findings.description: DEC-SYE-005 reserves 0.5 ms per cycle for the run-time CRC but leaves the rest of the SYS-SUP-052 processor budget to later stages. No feasibility analysis shows that the software CRC in SYE-SUP-064, other supervision work and their timing interactions fit the 0.5 ms per cycle and 10% per second limits.
findings.requested_change: Allocate the remaining timing budget across the relevant elements and provide a supported feasibility analysis, or record the missing platform measurements or decisions as blocking open points.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-032 requires fault-free operating time to be measured with bounded under-count and no over-count. SYE-SUP-005 provides the time base and SYE-SUP-025 performs counting, but SYE-SUP-053 omits the fault manager from its endpoints. The architecture also lacks an identified interface for the fault manager's retained state and for status and history passed to diagnostic communication.
findings.requested_change: Identify and specify the time-base, retained-state, status and history connections, including their endpoints and the timing and data needed to meet the cited requirements.

findings.description: SYE-SUP-022 through SYE-SUP-027 run on the same microcontroller as the supervised software. SYE-SUP-002 has an independent clock, but the architecture does not analyse interference between the supervisor, application tasks and shared processor or show how a stalled supervisor causes watchdog servicing to stop.
findings.requested_change: Describe the independence and interference assumptions and show how failures or resource contention in the supervised software cannot indefinitely prevent the watchdog reaction, or record the unresolved evidence as an open point.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-054 requires testable system requirements to be verifiable on Renode or host tests. OP-SYE-004 leaves GPIO, serial, reset-flag and fault-injection observation or stimulation mechanisms unestablished, so the architecture has not shown that its proposed integration observations are available.
findings.requested_change: Establish feasible observation and stimulation mechanisms for the required verification environment, or make the missing environment capability a blocking open point.

findings.description: SYE-SUP-004 says use of the CRC peripheral is conditional on confirming its algorithm capability, whereas SYE-SUP-052 describes the peripheral interface as the interface for the integrity checks without stating that condition. SYE-SUP-064 and SYE-SUP-065 instead allocate the current computation to software.
findings.requested_change: Make the conditional status of SYE-SUP-052 explicit and align its allocation with the software CRC path and OP-SYE-002.
